easy.def: A car that you pay to ride in.
examples: We took a cab.
The cab came fast.
The cab driver waved.

more.def: A car with a driver that you pay to take you somewhere.
examples: We took a cab to the airport.
The cab driver knew the way.
A yellow cab pulled up to the curb.

easy.def: A sweet baked food.
examples: I ate a piece of cake.
We have cake on my birthday.
Mom baked a cake.

more.def: A sweet food made from flour, sugar and eggs that is baked in an oven.
examples: Dad baked a chocolate cake for my birthday.
She cut the cake into twelve slices.
The cake had pink frosting and sprinkles.

easy.def: To say something in a loud voice.
examples: I call to my dog.
Mom called us for dinner.
She calls from the yard.

more.def: To shout or speak loudly to get someone's attention.
examples: The coach called to the players from the sideline.
I heard someone calling my name across the field.
Please call the children inside when it starts to rain.

easy.def: To use a phone to talk to someone.
examples: I will call Grandma.
He called me last night.
Call me later.

more.def: To telephone someone.
examples: I will call my cousin to wish her a happy birthday.
She called the library to ask when it closes.
Please call us when you get to the airport.

easy.def: To give a name to someone or something.
examples: We call our cat Mittens.
They called the baby Leo.
What do you call this plant?

more.def: To give a name to someone or something, or to describe it with a certain word.
examples: People call that big yellow flower a sunflower.
We called our new puppy Biscuit.
Scientists call baby frogs tadpoles.

easy.def: Quiet and not upset.
examples: Take a deep breath and stay calm.
The sea is calm today.
Mom's voice is calm and soft.

more.def: Peaceful and quiet; not excited, worried, or angry.
examples: The lake was calm and smooth after the storm passed.
The pilot stayed calm during the bumpy flight.
Soft music helps me feel calm before bed.

easy.def: A machine that takes pictures.
examples: Smile for the camera.
Dad has a camera.
The camera is on.

more.def: A device that takes photographs or records video.
examples: I took a photo of the sunset with my camera.
The scientist set up a camera to film the owls.
Smile at the camera!

easy.def: Colors that help an animal hide.
examples: The frog's green skin is camouflage in the grass.
A tiger's stripes are camouflage in tall grass.
The moth uses camouflage to hide on a tree.

more.def: Colors or patterns that help an animal or thing blend in with what is around it.
examples: A snowshoe hare's white fur is good camouflage in winter.
The soldiers wore green and brown camouflage in the forest.
An octopus can change color for camouflage.

easy.def: A place where people sleep outdoors.
examples: We set up camp.
The camp is by the lake.
The camp has tents.

more.def: A place outdoors where people stay in tents or cabins.
examples: We set up camp by the river.
She spent two weeks at summer camp.
The hikers returned to camp at sunset.

easy.def: To sleep outdoors in a tent.
examples: We camp in summer.
They camped by the lake.
I like to camp.

more.def: To stay outdoors for a few days, usually in a tent.
examples: We camped by the lake for the weekend.
My family likes to camp in the mountains.
They camped under the stars.

easy.def: Able to do something.
examples: I can tie my shoes.
Birds can fly.
Can you swim?

more.def: Used to show that someone is able to do something or is allowed to do it.
examples: Cheetahs can run faster than any other land animal.
You can borrow my pencil if you give it back.
Can I help you carry those books?

easy.def: A round metal container for food or drinks.
examples: I opened a can of soup.
Put the can in the bin.
The can was empty.

more.def: A metal container, often shaped like a tube, that is used to hold food, drinks, or paint.
examples: He used a can of paint to color the fence.
The class collected cans of food for families in need.
She rinsed the soup can before putting it in the recycling.

easy.def: To say that something will not happen.
examples: They canceled the party.
The game was canceled.
We canceled the trip.

more.def: To decide that something planned will not happen.
examples: They canceled the picnic because of rain.
The school canceled the game.
We canceled our trip.

easy.def: A sweet treat.
examples: I like candy.
The candy is sweet.
He ate a piece of candy.

more.def: A sweet food made from sugar, often small and sold in pieces.
examples: She bought a bag of candy at the store.
The candy melted in the sun.
We got candy at the parade.

easy.def: The leader of a ship or a team.
examples: The captain steered.
She is the team captain.
The captain waved.

more.def: The person in charge of a ship, plane, or sports team.
examples: The captain steered the ship safely into the harbor.
Our soccer team chose Maya as captain.
The pilot is the captain of the plane.

easy.def: To catch.
examples: The net will capture the fish.
I captured a bug in a jar.
The police captured the robber.

more.def: To catch and hold a person, animal, or thing.
examples: The photographer captured a picture of the eagle in flight.
The scientists captured the bird, tagged it, and let it go.
In the game, you capture the other team's flag to win.

easy.def: A vehicle with four wheels that people ride in.
examples: We ride in a car.
The red car stopped.
Dad washed the car.

more.def: A road vehicle with an engine and four wheels that carries a few people.
examples: Our family drove the car to the lake for the weekend.
The car stopped at the red light.
She buckled her seat belt as soon as she got into the car.

easy.def: A piece of stiff paper with a message.
examples: I made a card for Mom.
She sent a birthday card.
We got a card in the mail.

more.def: A piece of stiff paper with a picture or message, sent for a special day.
examples: We made a card for Grandma's birthday.
She sent a thank-you card to her teacher.
A get-well card arrived in the mail.

easy.def: One of a set used in games.
examples: Pick a card.
We play a card game.
A card fell on the floor.

more.def: One of a set of small pieces of stiff paper used to play games.
examples: She dealt seven cards to each player.
A deck of cards has fifty-two cards.
He drew a card and smiled.

easy.def: To feel that someone or something matters.
examples: I care about my friend.
She cares for her pet.
He cared a lot.

more.def: To feel that something is important, or to look after someone or something.
examples: I care about my friends, and I listen when they are upset.
She cares for the class hamster on weekends.
Do you care which game we play?

easy.def: Being careful or looking after someone.
examples: Take care.
The baby needs care.
Handle it with care.

more.def: Close attention to avoid mistakes or harm, or the act of looking after someone or something.
examples: Carry the eggs with care so that they do not break.
The nurse gave the patient good care.
A garden needs a lot of care in the summer.

easy.def: The job you do for many years.
examples: She has a career as a nurse.
He wants a career in sports.
My mom has a career in teaching.

more.def: The work a person does for much of their life.
examples: She has a career as a pilot.
He wants a career in music.
Her career as a teacher lasted forty years.

easy.def: Trying hard to stay safe and not make a mistake.
examples: Be careful with the hot soup.
Be careful on the icy steps.
I am careful with my glasses.

more.def: Paying close attention so that you avoid danger or mistakes.
examples: She was careful not to step on the wet paint.
He made a careful drawing of the bird's feathers.
Be careful to check your answers before you turn in the test.

easy.def: To hold something and take it somewhere.
examples: I carry my bag.
Dad carried me upstairs.
Ants carry crumbs.

more.def: To hold something while you move it from one place to another.
examples: She carried a tray of cups to the table.
Ants can carry food many times their own weight.
Please carry the groceries into the kitchen.

easy.def: A box or cover to hold something.
examples: I put it in a case.
The glasses are in a case.
She has a pencil case.

more.def: A box or cover that holds or protects something.
examples: He put his glasses in their case.
The museum keeps the old coins in a glass case.
I keep my markers in a zip-up pencil case.

easy.def: An example of something that happens.
examples: In this case, we wait.
It is a rare case.
That is not the case.

more.def: A particular situation or example of something.
examples: In this case, the answer is yes, because the rule says so.
It was a case of mixed-up names.
The detective worked on a very strange case.

easy.def: Money in coins and bills.
examples: I paid in cash.
Do you have cash?
She had cash in her pocket.

more.def: Money in the form of coins and bills, not a card or check.
examples: He paid for the toy in cash.
She keeps some cash in her wallet.
The shop takes cash or cards.

easy.def: A small pet with soft fur and whiskers.
examples: The cat sleeps on the bed.
My cat purrs.
A cat chased the mouse.

more.def: A small furry animal that is often kept as a pet and has sharp claws and whiskers.
examples: The cat curled up on the warm windowsill.
A cat can jump much higher than its own height.
Our cat chases a ball of yarn.

easy.def: To grab something that is moving.
examples: Catch the ball.
The dog caught the stick.
I can catch it.

more.def: To grab and hold something that is moving through the air.
examples: Can you catch the ball when I throw it?
The goalie caught the ball with both hands.
She caught the leaf as it fell from the tree.

easy.def: To get on a bus or train in time.
examples: We catch the bus.
She caught the train.
Hurry and catch it.

more.def: To get on a bus, train, or plane before it leaves.
examples: We ran to catch the school bus.
He caught the early train to the city.
If we hurry, we can catch the last boat.

easy.def: To get sick from a germ.
examples: I caught a cold.
He caught the flu.
Do not catch cold.

more.def: To become sick with something, such as a cold.
examples: My brother caught a cold after playing in the rain.
She caught the flu and stayed home for a week.
Wash your hands to avoid catching germs.

easy.def: To make something happen.
examples: Rain can cause floods.
The wind caused the door to shut.
Ice causes slips.

more.def: To make something happen, or to be the reason that it happens.
examples: Heavy rain can cause a river to overflow.
The loud noise caused the baby to wake up.
Too much sun can cause a sunburn.

easy.def: The reason something happens.
examples: What is the cause?
Rain is the cause.
The cause was a storm.

more.def: The thing that makes something happen.
examples: The cause of the traffic jam was a broken-down truck.
Scientists look for the cause of the strange noise.
A spark was the cause of the small fire.
